chart_check: Two panels of bar charts — left shows total crashes per weekday with count and % labels, right shows crashes per occurrence of that weekday; y-axes are labelled with units and start at 0, nothing is cut off or overlapping, and every plotted label matches values.csv (304,518/14.3% … 257,544/12.1%; 449, 462, 458, 470, 500, 425, 380). Shares sum to 100%, n = 2,132,218 matches the sum of the seven counts, n_days sums to 4,748 days (2013-01-01 to 2025-12-31), and all avg_crashes_per_day values recompute correctly.
answer: Across 2013–2025 NYC recorded 2,132,218 crashes, and the weekly pattern climbs to Friday — Wed (311,111) dipping just below Tue (313,488) along the way — then drops over the weekend: Fri is the peak (338,800; 15.9%; ~500/day), Thu next (318,376; 470/day), then Tue (313,488), Wed (311,111) and Mon the softest weekday (304,518; 449/day), while Sat falls to 288,381 (425/day) and Sunday is the clear low at 257,544 (12.1%; ~380/day) — Friday sees 32% more crashes than Sunday, and weekdays (5 of 7 days) carry 74.4% of all crashes.
